chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you stand in the first two rak'ahs and have not yet recited the Tashahhud, if you remember before bowing, sit and recite the Tashahhud; and if you do not remember until you bow, continue in your prayer as you are. When you finish, prostrate two prostrations without bowing in them, then recite the Tashahhud that you missed."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to recite the Tashahhud in the first two rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific jurisprudence of *sahw* (forgetfulness) regarding the omission of the Tashahhud in the first two rak'ahs. It establishes a clear distinction between remembering before *ruku'* (requiring a return to sit) and after *ruku'* (requiring continuation followed by *sajdat al-khata'*), reflecting the Imami school's precise approach to correcting ritual errors without invalidating the prayer. The instruction to perform the missed Tashahhud after the final salam, accompanied by two prostrations without bowing, underscores the practical application of compensatory acts in Shia fiqh.}
